content.comment_body: Hello, can anyone share if there's an 'analog amplifier' block available in the [product_name] device? I want to create a program directly on the hardware, not using [product_name] programming software, but I can't find this specific block. Thanks in advance.
Here is a link to the manual: [url]. Refer to chapter 4.4.20. The function should be listed under Special Functions. Best regards, [user_name].

The availability of the analog amplifier block depends on your [product_name] hardware. If you have an older version, it's not present. This block has been supported since [version_no]. Hope this clarifies.

I've checked the manual, but I'm not seeing this function block in my [product_name]. I'm unsure why, since all the other blocks are present. If anyone has more information, please let me know. I currently use a [article_no] [product_name].

The analog amplifier block is available in [article_no] hardware, but you need to navigate to it. When programming without software, start from the output and work backwards to the input. Example: AI1 <-- analog amplifier <-- AQ1. In edit mode, go to: 1) AQ1 or AQ2 (analog output); 2) press OK; 3) select analog function; 4) press OK; 5) choose analog amplifier; 6) press OK twice; 7) Choose Connector; 8) select the AI channel connected to your sensor; 9) press OK; 10) press OK again to edit parameters. Pay attention to where the cursor is blinking, as this is what you confirm with OK.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unclear about finding the 'analog amplifier' function block within the [product_name] device itself, despite documentation confirming its availability in newer [version_no]. The main challenge is in accessing and configuring the block directly on the hardware without relying on [product_name] programming software. Users desire more straightforward navigation and access to special function blocks when working on the physical device.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to easily locate and use the analog amplifier block directly on the [product_name] hardware, just like other function blocks, without dependency on external programming tools.
